title: Contract evolution runbook for streaming + tool interfaces and structured outputs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: produce an actionable runbook and deliverables to evolve the Core API contract for streaming responses, tool/function calling, and structured outputs with minimal customer disruption. Scope covers behavior flag orchestration, graduated deprecation windows, deterministic regression harnesses, and telemetry-driven rollback criteria. Non-goals: changes to model weights or model-internal tokenization algorithms, and client SDK refactors beyond thin compatibility shims. Deliverables: (1) runbook for staged toggles and canary criteria, (2) migration guide for clients and partners, (3) regression test suite and replay harness, (4) telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds, (5) sample SDK compatibility adapter. Rationale: recent experiments to tighten structured-output schema and to normalize streaming chunk headers broke a subset of legacy clients in shadow runs. We need a repeatable, low-risk path to roll forward these contract changes while collecting guardrail metrics and offering clear migration steps for integrators.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook published and reviewed by Eng/UX/SRE/Legal
Canary flow implemented so 1% of traffic runs new contract with fallback to old behavior on mismatch
Regression harness reproduces 95%+ of past streaming/toolcall bug classes against saved production traces
Migration guide and sample compatibility adapter published in docs with at least one partner migration validated
Telemetry dashboards with automated alerts for error-rate, client-side parse-failures, latency regressions, and percent-of-clients-still-on-legacy-schema

notes: Rollout strategy summary: feature flag gating with three phases — developer opt-in (client SDK flags), canary (1-5% traffic), staged ramp to 50% with partial regressions allowed, final cutover after 90 days or when parse-failure < 0.1% for two consecutive weeks.

Regression harness details: replay saved production request traces with both old and new serializers, run golden prompt suite, perform fuzzing focused on nested structured-output corners and truncated streaming frames, and run end-to-end tool-call invocations against test tool endpoints to verify invocation envelope stability.

Client migration guidance highlights: include 'x-rw-api-schema-version' in streaming frames, support legacy streaming frame headers for 90-day window, provide compatibility adapter example that translates between v1 and v2 structured envelopes, and highlight potential token-cost implications when using dual-run/tracing.
Abort criteria: immediate rollback if canary parse-failures exceed 1% or user-facing error rate increases > 0.5% absolute for two consecutive 5-minute windows; escalate to oncall and PM for decision.

Open questions: need a minimal e2e test harness for on-prem Private deployments (air-gapped) that cannot contact our telemetry backplane — possible solution: offline log artifacts and partner-run replay harness.
Next steps: finalize runbook doc, merge shim prototype PR, onboard first partner for pilot, and create an SDK sample PR that demonstrates opt-in header usage.
